UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection) embeds high-dimensional
data in two dimensions, preserving which observations are close to each other.
ggumap computes the embedding *inside* a ggplot2 layer, so there is no
separate step and no data wrangling between computation and plot.

```{r setup}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggumap)
```

## A first plot

`geom_umap()` uses all numeric columns as features and draws points.
Aesthetics like `colour` work as usual; they are carried along, but do not
influence the embedding.

```{r first}
penguins <- palmerpenguins::penguins

ggplot(penguins, aes(colour = species)) +
  geom_umap(na.rm = TRUE)
```

The numeric columns of `penguins` are measured in different units (body mass
in grams dominates the distances), so standardise them with `scale = TRUE`.
`theme_umap()` removes axis text and ticks, since UMAP coordinates have no
meaning of their own.

```{r scaled}
ggplot(penguins, aes(colour = species)) +
  geom_umap(scale = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  theme_umap()
```

## Selecting features

`features` takes the same syntax as `dplyr::select()`. Here `year` is left
out:

```{r features}
ggplot(penguins, aes(colour = species, shape = sex)) +
  geom_umap(features = bill_length_mm:body_mass_g, scale = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  theme_umap()
```

## Any geom, several layers

`stat_umap()` can render the embedding with any geom. Layers with the same
data and settings share one embedding: it is computed once and cached.

```{r layers}
cars <- transform(mtcars, model = rownames(mtcars))

ggplot(cars, aes(label = model, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_umap(scale = TRUE, n_neighbors = 5) +
  stat_umap(
    geom = "text", scale = TRUE, n_neighbors = 5,
    size = 2.5, vjust = -0.8, show.legend = FALSE,
    check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.15)) +
  labs(colour = "cylinders") +
  theme_umap()
```

```{r density}
ggplot(penguins) +
  stat_umap(
    geom = "density_2d_filled", features = bill_length_mm:body_mass_g,
    scale = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE, contour_var = "ndensity"
  ) +
  theme_umap()
```

## Computed variables

Besides the coordinates `UMAP1` and `UMAP2`, the stat computes `knn_dist`, the
mean distance of each observation to its nearest neighbours in the input
space. Large values point at outliers.

```{r knn-dist}
ggplot(penguins) +
  geom_umap(
    aes(colour = after_stat(knn_dist)),
    features = bill_length_mm:body_mass_g, scale = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c() +
  theme_umap()
```

## Facets

By default one embedding is computed for the whole layer, and each facet shows
a subset of it. With `scope = "panel"`, every panel gets its own embedding.

```{r facets, fig.height = 3}
ggplot(penguins, aes(colour = sex)) +
  geom_umap(features = bill_length_mm:body_mass_g, scale = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(vars(species)) +
  theme_umap()
```

## Tuning UMAP

The most important parameters are

* `n_neighbors`: the size of the neighbourhood. Small values emphasise local
  structure, large values global structure.
* `min_dist`: how tightly points may be packed together.
* `metric`: the distance in input space, e.g. `"cosine"` or `"manhattan"`.

```{r tuning}
ggplot(penguins, aes(colour = species)) +
  geom_umap(
    features = bill_length_mm:body_mass_g, scale = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE,
    n_neighbors = 50, min_dist = 0.8
  ) +
  theme_umap()
```

Rarely needed parameters live in `umap_control()`.

## Reproducibility

The stat derives its random seed from the data, so a plot looks the same every
time it is drawn. Pass `seed` to choose another layout:

```{r seed, fig.height = 3}
ggplot(penguins, aes(colour = species)) +
  geom_umap(
    features = bill_length_mm:body_mass_g, scale = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE,
    seed = 2
  ) +
  theme_umap()
```

UMAP runs in parallel on `umap_threads()` threads (half of your cores by
default; set the option `ggumap.n_threads` to change this). With the default
`flavour = "0.5"`, multi-threaded results are not bit-for-bit reproducible
across sessions; use `n_threads = 1`, or `flavour = "0.6"` which is
deterministic for a fixed number of threads.

## Outside of plots

`umap_embed()` returns the embedding as a data frame, for example to use it in
further analyses:

```{r embed}
emb <- umap_embed(penguins, bill_length_mm:body_mass_g, scale = TRUE, seed = 1)
head(emb)
```
